_note: Hand-written neutral summaries (written 2026-10-23 by the research agent from the documents themselves) for Green Party documents and announcements that are not, or not only, covered by policy.nz statements. Each becomes an entry with summary_source 'archive' in policies.json. 'group' is a policy.nz top-level topic group.

manifesto-2026-full-pdf.statement: 2026 election manifesto: 'A Green government. For all of us.' (38 policy chapters)
manifesto-2026-full-pdf.summary: The party's 43-page (23 PDF spreads) 2026 election manifesto, launched at its AGM on 26 July 2026. It frames the campaign around three priorities (affordable living, healthy nature and 'real democracy'), funded by taxes on the very wealthy and large corporations alongside an income tax cut for most earners, and sets out a short numbered 'Our plan' list in each of 38 policy chapters (Children to Zero waste). Every 'Our plan' commitment is listed individually below under its topic.

maori-manifesto-2026-pdf.summary: A separate Māori-focused version of the 2026 manifesto (34 pages) organised around taiao, tāngata, tāhua and rangatiratanga. It opens with a 'Kaupapa Māori — by Māori, for Māori' chapter and then restates each manifesto chapter with emphasis on Te Tiriti o Waitangi, tino rangatiratanga and outcomes for whānau, hapū and iwi.

manifesto-2026-easy-read-pdf.statement: Easy Read version of the 2026 manifesto
manifesto-2026-easy-read-pdf.summary: An Easy Read (plain-language, illustrated) summary of the 2026 manifesto published in August 2026 for disabled people and others who prefer simplified text. It points readers to the full manifesto online.

tax-policy-2026-a-tax-system-for-all-of-.statement: Tax policy 'A tax system for all of us': wealth tax, capital acquisitions tax, higher tax on big corporates, bank levy, and income tax cuts for 96% of earners
tax-policy-2026-a-tax-system-for-all-of-.summary: The 12-page tax plan (announced 21 June 2026). Revenue measures: a 2.5% tax on the net assets of the super-rich above $10 million (family homes exempt); a capital acquisitions tax on gifts and inheritances over $1 million (family farms and homes exempt); a 33% company tax rate for the largest 0.7% of companies while small and medium firms stay at 28%; a 0.06% levy on the liabilities of the four big banks; enforcing a 5% withholding tax on big tech profits sent offshore; and reversing the coalition's landlord interest-deductibility and bright-line changes. Income tax: a $10,000 tax-free threshold, new stepped brackets and a 45% rate above $160,000. The party's own Parliamentary-Library-based modelling puts the net gain at about $5.1-5.7 billion a year (2027/28-2030/31).

drink-swim-fish-policy-2026.statement: 'Drink Swim Fish' freshwater and oceans policy
drink-swim-fish-policy-2026.summary: A 4-page water policy (announced 6 July 2026) aimed at safe drinking water, swimmable rivers and healthier oceans: science-based national freshwater limits including lower nitrate limits, stronger wastewater-discharge rules, phasing out synthetic nitrogen fertiliser, phasing out bottom trawling and other destructive fishing, protecting at least 30% of oceans, and reviewing the fisheries quota system.

power-for-all-of-us-policy-2026.statement: 'Power for all of us' energy policy: Kiwipower, Warmer Kiwi Homes expansion, community energy and zero-interest solar loans
power-for-all-of-us-policy-2026.summary: The 12-page energy policy (announced 20 July 2026). It proposes 'Kiwipower', a publicly owned company to contract and build electricity firming; an expanded Warmer Kiwi Homes insulation/heating programme; $200m for community-owned energy; a government-backed Clean Energy Loans Scheme (modelled as zero-interest, tied to the property) for rooftop solar and other home energy upgrades; and other electricity-market changes. It includes four-year cost tables and says spending would be funded by the proposed super-rich tax.

kiwipower-explainer-2026.statement: Establish Kiwipower, a publicly owned electricity firming company
kiwipower-explainer-2026.summary: A 6-page explainer for the proposed publicly owned firming company 'Kiwipower': it would contract access to existing hydro/thermal firming, invest in new renewable firming and storage (geothermal, biomass, batteries, small pumped hydro, demand response) and sell firming at fair prices to independent retailers and large users. Costed at $412.6m opex and $568m capex over 2027/28-2030/31, to be established by the end of 2027. (Image-only PDF; text transcribed by hand.)

te-waonui-a-tane-policy-2026.statement: Te Waonui a Tāne: an ongoing, protected funding source for marae
te-waonui-a-tane-policy-2026.summary: An 11-page policy (announced 9 August 2026) to recognise and resource marae as social and cultural infrastructure. It proposes a Rangatiratanga Trust with a $2.44 billion Crown funding input, including a $2 billion intergenerational fund (Te Tōtara Haemata) and annual restoration funding for marae, governed with regional marae representation.

youth-jobs-guarantee-policy-2026.statement: Youth Jobs Guarantee: a job or training pathway for every 16-24-year-old out of work for six months
youth-jobs-guarantee-policy-2026.summary: A 7-page jobs policy (published October 2026) guaranteeing every 16-to-24-year-old who has been out of work for six months a pathway into a locally based job or training, delivered with councils and building on the Mayors Taskforce for Jobs. The document's indicative costings rise from $604m in the first year to $1,631m in the fourth.

ai-policy-2026-safe-sovereign-ai.statement: 'Safe, sovereign AI': regulate artificial intelligence for the public good
ai-policy-2026-safe-sovereign-ai.summary: An 8-page AI plan (announced 12 October 2026). It proposes rules so that AI does not replace human or democratic decision-making (no fully automated decisions with substantive effects in public services), protects data sovereignty, privacy and creators' work, operates within environmental limits (including controls on data centres), shares benefits rather than concentrating them, and is transparent and accountable.

affordable-food-for-all-of-us-policy-202.statement: 'Affordable food for all of us': KiwiMart public supermarket chain, stronger grocery regulation and a Fair Food Fund
affordable-food-for-all-of-us-policy-202.summary: A 15-page food-system policy (announced 6 September 2026). It proposes a publicly owned supermarket chain 'KiwiMart' (estimated acquisition and capitalisation cost about $2.8bn, citing an estimate of $1.3bn to buy 120 stores and two distribution centres), more Commerce Commission funding and higher penalties for grocery-sector breaches, a $150m Fair Food Fund for community food security, and more funding for regional food providers.

paid-placements-apprenticeships-policy-2.statement: Paid placements for trainee nurses, teachers and social workers; abolish the training wage for apprentices
paid-placements-apprenticeships-policy-2.summary: A 4-page workforce policy (16-17 October 2026): a universal weekly payment for students during compulsory practical placements (nursing, teaching, social work and similar), relocation support, abolition of the training-wage exemption so apprentices get at least the minimum wage, a grant for apprentices' tools, and more pastoral support. Indicative costs are about $75-80m and $117m a year for the two parts.

hauraki-gulf-restoration-of-high-protect.statement: Bill to remove ring-net fishing exemption from Hauraki Gulf high protection areas
hauraki-gulf-restoration-of-high-protect.summary: A 6-page draft member's bill (released 6 October 2026) amending the Hauraki Gulf / Tīkapa Moana Marine Protection Act 2025 to remove the exemption that allows ring-net fishing in high protection areas, and to allow further management actions, developed with iwi, where protection objectives are not being met.

green-budget-2025.statement: Green Budget 2025: the Greens' costed alternative Budget (2025)
green-budget-2025.summary: The party's 44-page alternative Budget published in 2025 (not a 2026 election document, but the basis of several 2026 policies). It sets out spending on health (free GP and dental care), families, ending poverty, climate, oceans, nature, a green industrial strategy, transport, housing and energy, funded by wealth, corporate and other tax changes, with a fiscal summary. Cited by policy.nz for the free-ECE policy.

policy_pdfs_summary.agriculture-policy-2025-2026: Standing party policy on farming: support farmers to reduce environmental harm and emissions, uphold Te Tiriti in sector governance, fair prices for producers, better data, and treat farm animals as sentient.
policy_pdfs_summary.animal-welfare-2025-2026: Standing party policy to align animal-welfare law with animals' needs (nutrition, environment, health, behaviour, mental state), strengthen oversight, reduce systemic exploitation of animals and recognise Māori kaitiaki relationships with animals.
policy_pdfs_summary.arts-culture-heritage-policy-2014-2026: Standing party policy to resource the arts and heritage sector, protect traditional and contemporary Māori art, and expand arts education and platforms in schools and communities.
policy_pdfs_summary.biodiversity-environmental-regenration-p: Standing party policy on conservation: protect threatened indigenous species from pests, disease and human activity, take a holistic approach to restoring ecosystems, and support tangata whenua as kaitiaki.
policy_pdfs_summary.business-policy-2025-2026: Standing party policy on business: reform regulators, require accessibility, support the Māori economy and new business models, promote local business and co-invest in skills and research.
policy_pdfs_summary.childrens-2013-2026: Standing party policy on children: reform social support, extend paid parental leave, reform Working for Families and lift minimum entitlements with the aim of eliminating child poverty, and improve cross-government child protection.
policy_pdfs_summary.climate-change-policy-2022-2026: Standing party climate policy: Te Tiriti-based solutions, energy efficiency and democratisation, low-carbon transport, a rapid fossil-fuel phase-out, more plant-based and resilient farming, an economy that does not rely on growth, and adaptation planning that prioritises the most vulnerable.
policy_pdfs_summary.communities-of-colour-policy-2025: Standing party policy on working in partnership with people of colour and ethnic communities to meet their needs and aspirations and tackle racism.
policy_pdfs_summary.community-economy-policy-2011-2025: Standing party policy on regional development, local economies and procurement, and on government relationships with, and funding of, the community and voluntary sector.
policy_pdfs_summary.digital-policy-2025: Standing party policy on equitable access to digital technology and data, with a harm-based approach to social media, AI and quantum computing, Te Tiriti and privacy/online-safety protections.
policy_pdfs_summary.drug-policy-2016-2026: Standing party policy taking a harm-minimisation, health-based approach to alcohol and other drugs instead of criminal prohibition: accessible addiction treatment, a legal regulated cannabis market and drug-checking/education.
policy_pdfs_summary.emergency-management-policy-2025-2026: Standing party policy on civil defence: resource agencies and communities to prepare for and respond to emergencies, strengthen infrastructure resilience, use local and Māori knowledge, prioritise vulnerable people and fund managed retreat from high-risk areas.
policy_pdfs_summary.energy-policy-2022-2025: Standing party energy policy: reform electricity markets, support community energy ownership, legislate fossil-fuel reductions, electrify transport and heat, and expand efficiency and renewable supply.
policy_pdfs_summary.food-policy-2024-2026: Standing party policy on the right to safe, affordable food, including Māori food practices, and a national food-system strategy for local resilience, less waste and lower emissions.
policy_pdfs_summary.forestry-policy-2025: Standing party forestry policy: long-term carbon storage and biodiversity, community-protecting forestry rules, value-added wood processing and kaupapa Māori forestry governance.
policy_pdfs_summary.freshwater-policy-2022-2026: Standing party freshwater policy: Te Tiriti-centred, holistic protection and restoration of rivers, lakes, aquifers and wetlands.
policy_pdfs_summary.global-affairs-policy-2020-2025: Standing party foreign-policy statement supporting an international rules-based order, human rights, environmental protection, disarmament and non-violent conflict resolution.
policy_pdfs_summary.government-economy-policy-2024-2026: Standing party economic policy: a fairer tax system, universal public services and infrastructure, living within planetary limits, Māori economic justice and more public ownership and direct service provision.
policy_pdfs_summary.housing-and-sustainable-communities-poli: Standing party housing policy: a large government-run public housing programme, more Māori housing, accessible housing for disabled people, lower building emissions and regenerative urban development; housing treated as a right.
policy_pdfs_summary.human-rights-policy-2024-2026: Standing party human-rights policy: strengthen tangata whenua rights, protect future generations, extend human-rights law and treaty commitments, and give courts and human-rights bodies more power.
policy_pdfs_summary.immigration-policy-2017-2026: Standing party immigration policy: fair, flexible selection, dignity and fair employment for migrants, family reunification, and a firm commitment to refugees and asylum seekers.
policy_pdfs_summary.justice-policy-2025-2026: Standing party justice policy: a system grounded in Te Tiriti and tikanga, prioritising restorative justice, rehabilitation, prevention and mental-health responses, tackling bias and improving access to justice.
policy_pdfs_summary.land-use-and-soils-policy-2022-2025: Standing party policy on land use: manage land under Te Tiriti, protect and regenerate soils, and minimise the impacts of mining.
policy_pdfs_summary.livelihoods-policy-2025: Standing party policy on income support: an adequate, accessible and dignified welfare system recognising unpaid work, regulation of lenders and debt help for low-income households.
policy_pdfs_summary.marine-policy-2022-2026: Standing party oceans policy: Te Tiriti-based marine governance, precautionary ecosystem-based management, and protection and regeneration of marine ecosystems.
policy_pdfs_summary.media-policy-2014-2026: Standing party media policy: support independent and community media, publicly owned broadcasting and funding for local content, prioritising under-served audiences including Māori and children.
policy_pdfs_summary.overseas-new-zealanders-policy-2022-2026: Standing party policy on the New Zealand diaspora: services and rights for New Zealanders abroad, connection with home and participation (including voting).
policy_pdfs_summary.rainbow-policy-2022-2026: Standing party Rainbow policy built on the Te Whare Takatāpui framework, addressing discrimination and health and wellbeing for people of diverse genders, sexualities and sex characteristics.
policy_pdfs_summary.recreation-sport-policy-2016-2026: Standing party policy on equitable, publicly funded access to sport and recreation, and regulation of harmful activities including gambling.
policy_pdfs_summary.rural-communities-policy-2025: Standing party policy on rural communities: locally led solutions and access to public services that support rural wellbeing and ecosystems.
policy_pdfs_summary.security-defence-policy-2011-2026: Standing party defence and security policy: an independent, Pacific-oriented, non-violent approach; democratic oversight of security and intelligence agencies; and a defence force focused on peacekeeping, disaster relief, humanitarian work and environmental monitoring.
policy_pdfs_summary.seniors-policy-2025-2026: Standing party policy on older people: independence, connection, respect, equitable services and protection of cultural values for frail or dependent seniors.
policy_pdfs_summary.tagata-moana-policy-2022-2026: Standing party policy on Pacific peoples (Tagata Moana): community and cultural connections and support for decolonising and reindigenising Pacific identities.
policy_pdfs_summary.te-tiriti-o-waitangi-policy-2022-2026: Standing party policy on honouring Te Tiriti o Waitangi, upholding Māori rights and supporting Māori development and constitutional transformation.
policy_pdfs_summary.tourism-policy-2025: Standing party tourism policy: sustainable, low-emission, community-benefiting tourism and Māori cultural tourism under tikanga and tino rangatiratanga.
policy_pdfs_summary.trade-and-foreign-investment-policy-2011: Standing party trade policy: a global trade regime within ecological limits, enforceable human-rights and environmental protections, and democratic, transparent economic decision-making.
policy_pdfs_summary.waste-hazardous-substances-policy-2022-2: Standing party policy to move all sectors to a circular economy, eliminate unnecessary waste and hazardous substances, and manage the rest safely through reuse and recycling.
policy_pdfs_summary.womens-policy-2025-2026: Standing party women's policy: gender equity in leadership (including wāhine Māori), and protecting women and girls from harm at home, at work, in the community and online.
policy_pdfs_summary.workforce-policy-2020-2026: Standing party workforce policy: a just transition to a low-emissions economy, training and upskilling, workers' rights to secure income, safety and collective organising, and better work-life balance.
policy_pdfs_summary.youth-policy-2022-2025: Standing party youth policy on the rights, participation and wellbeing of young people.

web-greens-to-protect-employee-status-of.summary: 17 Nov 2025: the party said a Green government would honour the Supreme Court ruling that Uber drivers are employees and oppose legislation removing that status.

web-marama-davidson-mining-revocation-an.statement: Revoke fast-track consents/permits for coal, gold and seabed mining
web-marama-davidson-mining-revocation-an.summary: 17 Nov 2025: co-leader Marama Davidson announced that a Green government would revoke any consents or permits granted under the fast-track process for coal, gold and seabed mines.

web-pig-cruelty-won-t-stand-under-green-.statement: Phase out farrowing crates for pigs
web-pig-cruelty-won-t-stand-under-green-.summary: 12 Dec 2025: after the government passed a bill allowing farrowing crates for at least another 10 years, the party said a Green government would legislate the phase-out of farrowing crates.

web-greens-announce-bill-to-entrench-m-o.statement: Member's bill to entrench the Māori electorate seats
web-greens-announce-bill-to-entrench-m-o.summary: 23 Jan 2026: a member's bill in Hūhana Lyndon's name to entrench the Māori seats in electoral law, as the general electorate seats already are.

web-green-member-s-bill-to-recognise-the.statement: Member's bill to recognise whales (tohorā) as legal persons
web-green-member-s-bill-to-recognise-the.summary: 9 Feb 2026: Teanau Tuiono's member's bill to give whales legal personhood with rights including freedom of movement and a healthy environment.

web-greens-announce-plan-to-end-homeless.statement: 'A Home for Everybody' campaign: end homelessness, strengthen renters' rights
web-greens-announce-plan-to-end-homeless.summary: 26 Mar 2026: launch of the party's 'A Home for Everybody' housing campaign calling for an end to homelessness, stronger renters' rights and a large public-housing build.

web-greens-commit-to-tax-the-super-rich-.summary: 21 Jun 2026: release of 'A tax system for all of us' (wealth tax, capital acquisitions tax, higher tax on the biggest companies, bank levy, income tax cut for 96% of earners).

web-green-party-will-protect-public-cons.statement: Scrap the government's conservation law reform and rewrite conservation law
web-green-party-will-protect-public-cons.summary: 25 Jun 2026: the party said in government it would scrap the coalition's conservation reform and rewrite conservation law to give effect to Te Tiriti, centre indigenous-led stewardship and require the system to halt and reverse nature loss.

web-people-and-nature-first-in-greens-ri.statement: Announcement of the 'Drink Swim Fish' water policy
web-people-and-nature-first-in-greens-ri.summary: 6 Jul 2026: launch of the Drink Swim Fish policy programme on drinking water, swimmable rivers and healthy oceans.

web-green-party-calls-for-union-membersh.statement: Make union membership the default for new employees
web-green-party-calls-for-union-membersh.summary: 16 Jul 2026: the party backed an Automatic Union Membership member's bill amending the Employment Relations Act so new employees are union members by default, and said it would take the policy into the election.

web-green-party-launches-plan-to-cut-pow.statement: Announcement of the 'Power for all of us' energy policy
web-green-party-launches-plan-to-cut-pow.summary: 20 Jul 2026: launch of the energy policy including Kiwipower, expanded Warmer Kiwi Homes, community-owned power and rooftop solar support.

web-greens-bill-pushes-to-stop-supermark.statement: Require big supermarkets to donate edible surplus food (food waste bill)
web-greens-bill-pushes-to-stop-supermark.summary: 23 Jul 2026: Kahu Carter's Waste Minimisation (Food Waste) Amendment Bill, modelled on France's Garot law, would require large supermarkets to minimise food waste and partner with food-rescue groups.

web-call-for-one-year-pause-on-consentin.statement: One-year moratorium on consenting new AI data centres
web-call-for-one-year-pause-on-consentin.summary: 26 Jul 2026: call for a one-year pause on new AI data centre consents while rules on water, energy and community benefit are developed.

web-green-party-launches-2026-election-s.statement: Campaign slogan 'For all of us' and campaign priorities
web-green-party-launches-2026-election-s.summary: 26 Jul 2026: at the party AGM the co-leaders launched the slogan 'For all of us' and the manifesto; the release also discusses a Buy Kiwi Made-style approach to government purchasing.

web-new-bill-would-give-firefighters-wit.statement: Presumptive ACC cover for firefighters with occupational cancers
web-new-bill-would-give-firefighters-wit.summary: 27 Jul 2026: a member's bill to give eligible career and volunteer FENZ firefighters automatic ACC cover for cancers likely caused by their work.

web-green-party-announce-marae-funding-p.statement: Announcement of Te Waonui a Tāne marae funding policy
web-green-party-announce-marae-funding-p.summary: 9 Aug 2026: launch of the Te Waonui a Tāne policy for ongoing, protected marae funding.

web-new-bill-to-ban-supermarket-price-go.statement: Member's bill to ban grocery price gouging
web-new-bill-to-ban-supermarket-price-go.summary: 17 Aug 2026: the Commerce (Excessive Pricing in Retail Grocery Industry) Amendment Bill would make it unlawful for supermarkets to charge unreasonable prices for groceries.

web-green-party-announces-plan-for-free-.statement: Restore, extend and permanently fund Ka Ora, Ka Ako free school lunches
web-green-party-announces-plan-for-free-.summary: 20 Aug 2026: commitment to restore the original Ka Ora, Ka Ako school lunch model, extend it and fund it permanently, with locally prepared food.

web-greens-launch-plan-to-break-up-the-s.statement: Create KiwiMart, a publicly owned supermarket chain
web-greens-launch-plan-to-break-up-the-s.summary: 6 Sep 2026: launch of the 'Affordable food for all of us' policy, centred on a publicly owned supermarket chain, KiwiMart, to compete with the two major grocery chains.

web-green-party-pledge-to-remove-ai-from.statement: No AI or automated decisions on welfare payments or sanctions
web-green-party-pledge-to-remove-ai-from.summary: 11 Sep 2026: pledge that in government AI and automated decision-making would not be used to cancel, suspend or reduce benefits or impose sanctions.

web-ake-ake-ake-green-party-commits-200m.summary: 14 Sep 2026: commitment of $200m for te reo Māori initiatives in homes, schools and communities, including through Te Taura Whiri i te Reo Māori and Te Mātāwai.

web-greens-commit-to-undoing-attacks-on-.statement: Reverse the coalition's changes to conservation and environment laws
web-greens-commit-to-undoing-attacks-on-.summary: 19 Sep 2026: at the March for Nature, the party committed to managing conservation land for nature rather than profit and to restoring strong limits on environmentally harmful activity.

web-green-party-announce-plan-for-city-c.statement: Fairer commercial rent reviews and council auctions of long-empty shop leases
web-green-party-announce-plan-for-city-c.summary: 20 Sep 2026: plan to let market rent reviews lower as well as raise rents and to let councils auction leases of shops empty for over a year.

web-greens-announce-plan-to-get-big-mone.statement: Cap political donations at $30,000, ban corporate donations, create a lobbyist register
web-greens-announce-plan-to-get-big-mone.summary: 22 Sep 2026: a package of electoral-finance reforms including a $30,000 donation cap, a ban on company donations and a public register of lobbyists.

web-greens-commit-to-pay-equity-for-care.statement: Restore pre-2025 pay equity law and fund a care-worker settlement (~$1.1bn a year)
web-greens-commit-to-pay-equity-for-care.summary: 1 Oct 2026: commitment to restore pay-equity law to its pre-2025 form and set aside about $1.1 billion a year to settle the claim of around 65,000 care and support workers.

web-green-party-announce-plan-for-passen.statement: Intercity passenger rail: overnight Auckland-Wellington, Christchurch-Dunedin, Te Huia to Tauranga
web-green-party-announce-plan-for-passen.summary: 3 Oct 2026: plan for intercity passenger rail including an overnight Auckland-Wellington service, Christchurch-Dunedin trains and an improved, electrified Te Huia extended to Tauranga.

web-green-party-launches-the-transport-p.statement: 'Connect: Aotearoa' transport plan: free fares for some groups, $2 fare cap, bus lanes and rapid transit
web-green-party-launches-the-transport-p.summary: 4 Oct 2026: transport plan with free public transport for children, students, Community Service Card holders and Total Mobility users, a $2 fare cap for everyone else, bus lanes in the three main cities and mass rapid transit.

web-green-budget-early-childhood-educati.summary: 14 May 2025 (Green Budget 2025): plan to make early childhood education free and shift the sector away from for-profit provision.

web-green-budget-2025.summary: Landing page for the party's 2025 alternative Budget (see the Green Budget 2025 PDF).

web-one-year-on-from-apology-govt-still-.statement: Implement all 138 Royal Commission (Abuse in Care) recommendations
web-one-year-on-from-apology-govt-still-.summary: 12 Nov 2025: the party called for all 138 recommendations of the Royal Commission of Inquiry into Abuse in Care to be implemented and for boot camps to stop.

web-govt-s-empty-words-do-nothing-to-sto.statement: Recognise the State of Palestine immediately
web-govt-s-empty-words-do-nothing-to-sto.summary: 11 Aug 2025: the party called on the government to recognise Palestinian statehood immediately and take further action on Gaza.

scoop-greens-commercial-rent-reforms-tar.statement: Commercial leasing reforms applied to Christchurch's empty shops
scoop-greens-commercial-rent-reforms-tar.summary: 28 Sep 2026: Christchurch-focused release on the commercial leasing policy (council tools for long-empty shops, rent rules for small businesses).

scoop-greens-commit-to-funding-and-deliv.statement: Fund and deliver Auckland level-crossing removals
scoop-greens-commit-to-funding-and-deliv.summary: 5 Oct 2026: commitment to work with Auckland Council to fund and remove level crossings on the Western Line to unlock City Rail Link capacity.

scoop-greens-announce-plans-to-protect-t.statement: Hauraki Gulf protection: close commercial-fishing carve-outs, phase out bottom trawling, protect 30% by 2030
scoop-greens-announce-plans-to-protect-t.summary: 6 Oct 2026: plan to close the ring-net exemption in Hauraki Gulf high protection areas (draft bill attached), phase out bottom trawling and protect 30% of the Gulf by 2030.

scoop-greens-will-regulate-ai-for-the-pu.statement: Announcement of the 'Safe, sovereign AI' policy
scoop-greens-will-regulate-ai-for-the-pu.summary: 12 Oct 2026: release of the AI regulation policy (human decision-making, data sovereignty, environmental limits, shared benefits, transparency).

scoop-greens-economic-development-plan-w.statement: Economic development plan: rescope Investment Boost toward R&D (3% of GDP target)
scoop-greens-economic-development-plan-w.summary: 13 Oct 2026: economic development plan that the party says would create 284,000 jobs over four years (64,000 attributed to its policies on top of Treasury's forecast, per independent modelling it cites); it includes rescoping the Investment Boost tax incentive to drive research and development toward 3% of GDP.

scoop-greens-promise-to-reverse-national.statement: Cancel the $2.4bn of planned public service cuts
scoop-greens-promise-to-reverse-national.summary: 15 Oct 2026: commitment to cancel the public-service savings slated in Budget 2026 (stated as $2.39bn over 2026/27-2029/30; $3.17bn to cancel over 2027/28-2030/31).

scoop-greens-announce-paid-placements-fo.statement: Universal weekly payment for students on practical placements
scoop-greens-announce-paid-placements-fo.summary: 16 Oct 2026: a universal weekly payment for students during practical training for nursing, teaching, social work and similar roles, plus relocation support.

scoop-green-party-to-abolish-training-wa.statement: Abolish the training wage; more support for apprentices
scoop-green-party-to-abolish-training-wa.summary: 17 Oct 2026: commitment to remove the training-wage exemption so apprentices are paid at least the minimum wage, with more support for apprentices.
